```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, comment = "",
                      fig.path = "output/figures/", dev = "png", dpi = 300,
                      # knitr appends -1 to the chunk name; drop it
                      fig.process = function(f) {
                        g <- sub("-1\\.png$", ".png", f)
                        if (f != g) file.rename(f, g)
                        g
                      })
```

```{r packages}
library(tidyverse); library(sf); library(terra); library(marmap)
library(patchwork); library(rnaturalearth)

dir_derived <- "data/derived"; dir_fig <- "output/figures"
dir.create(dir_fig, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

BOX     <- list(lon = c(-98, -80), lat = c(18, 31))   # study area
MAP_LAT <- c(23.5, 31)                                # map extent, trimmed north of the Yucatan
SHELF_M <- 200                                        # shelf cut-off, metres
PEAK    <- c(6, 7)                                    # spawning-season months
SERIES  <- 1982:2016                                  # June-July sampling ends with the 2016 survey
SORTED  <- c("1", "2", "4", "D")
DWH     <- tibble(lon = -88.3660, lat = 28.7366)      # Deepwater Horizon wellhead

SIZE_LEVELS <- c("Small (<5 mm)", "Medium (5-15 mm)", "Large (>15 mm)")
SIZE_COLS   <- c("Small (<5 mm)" = "#D55E00", "Medium (5-15 mm)" = "#009E73",
                 "Large (>15 mm)" = "#0072B2")

theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.key.height = unit(10, "pt")))
```

Tables built by `01_data.Rmd`.

```{r read}
records <- read_csv(file.path(dir_derived, "cobia_records.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(size_class = factor(size_class, levels = SIZE_LEVELS))
lengths <- read_csv(file.path(dir_derived, "lengths.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(size = factor(size, levels = SIZE_LEVELS))
effort  <- read_csv(file.path(dir_derived, "effort.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

gulf <- records %>%
  filter(lon >= BOX$lon[1], lon <= BOX$lon[2], lat >= BOX$lat[1], lat <= BOX$lat[2])

# Numerator for any rate: the same gears and sorted status the effort pool is built from.
rates <- gulf %>% filter(gear %in% c("Bongo", "Neuston"), sort_ist %in% SORTED)
```

Bathymetry, isobaths and coastline, used by the three maps.

```{r basemap}
b <- getNOAA.bathy(BOX$lon[1], BOX$lon[2], BOX$lat[1], BOX$lat[2], resolution = 1, keep = TRUE,
                   path = dir_derived)
bathy <- as.xyz(b) %>% set_names(c("lon", "lat", "z")) %>% filter(z <= 0)
iso <- as.contour(rast(as.xyz(b), type = "xyz", crs = "EPSG:4326"),
                  levels = c(-200, -1000, -2000, -3000)) %>%
  st_as_sf() %>% st_set_crs(4326) %>% mutate(depth_m = -level)
land <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf") %>% st_make_valid() %>%
  st_crop(st_bbox(c(xmin = BOX$lon[1], xmax = BOX$lon[2],
                    ymin = BOX$lat[1], ymax = BOX$lat[2]), crs = st_crs(4326)))
map_frame <- list(coord_sf(xlim = BOX$lon, ylim = MAP_LAT, expand = FALSE), labs(x = NULL, y = NULL),
                  theme(panel.grid = element_blank()))
```

Catch rates divide by effort drawn from the same pool as the numerator, which here is sorted bongo
and neuston deployments. Comparisons between places are restricted to the months both were
sampled, because the surveys do not cover the same areas in every month.

```{r excluded}
sprintf("off-gear or unsorted, kept on the map but out of every rate: %d records, %.0f larvae",
        nrow(gulf) - nrow(rates), sum(gulf$n_total) - sum(rates$n_total))
```

# Distribution

Every record in the study box, coloured by the size class holding most of the tow. Descriptive, so
no effort is involved; the catch-rate maps come later.

```{r dist-numbers}
count(gulf, size_class)
gulf %>% slice_max(n_total, n = 3) %>% select(date, lat, lon, gear, n_total, n_meas)
```

Catches are heavily skewed. The median tow holds one larva and 79% hold one or two, but a neuston
tow off the delta on 8 June 2012 held 232, with the adjacent station the same day holding 38. The
whole sample was sorted in that case, so the number is real rather than a sub-sampling artefact.
Symbol size is binned for that reason: a continuous scale lets the one tow flatten everything else.

```{r main_distribution, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5.6}
p_dist <- ggplot() +
  geom_raster(data = bathy, aes(lon, lat, fill = z), interpolate = TRUE) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#1f3d6b", high = "#dbe9f6", name = "Depth (m)",
                      labels = function(x) -x, breaks = c(0, -3000, -6000),
                      guide = guide_colourbar(order = 3, barwidth = unit(48, "pt"),
                                              barheight = unit(6, "pt"))) +
  geom_sf(data = filter(iso, depth_m == 200), colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.35) +
  geom_sf(data = filter(iso, depth_m > 200), colour = "grey35", linewidth = 0.2,
          linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_sf(data = land, fill = "grey85", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_point(data = DWH, aes(lon, lat), shape = 8, size = 2.6, stroke = 0.9) +
  annotate("text", x = DWH$lon + 0.3, y = DWH$lat - 0.45, label = "DWH", size = 2.9, hjust = 0) +
  # smallest drawn last so they are not buried under the commoner medium tows
  geom_point(data = gulf %>% filter(!is.na(size_class)) %>%
               arrange(desc(as.integer(size_class)), desc(n_total)),
             aes(lon, lat, size = n_total, colour = size_class), alpha = 0.75) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = SIZE_COLS, name = "Most of the tow", drop = FALSE) +
  scale_size_binned(breaks = c(1, 5, 20, 100), range = c(1.2, 6.5), name = "Larvae per tow",
                    nice.breaks = FALSE) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(size = 3.6, alpha = 1)),
         size = guide_bins(order = 2, override.aes = list(colour = "grey45"))) +
  map_frame +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#dbe9f6"), legend.box = "horizontal",
        legend.box.just = "top", legend.spacing.x = unit(10, "pt"))
p_dist
```

# Season

Held to shelf stations and to 1982--2016, so the months sit on one footprint and one year range.
Gulf-wide effort mixes shelf and deep water in proportions that change month to month, and
June--July sampling ends in 2016 while September sampling continues.

```{r season-rates}
recs <- rates  %>% filter(sta_depth_m > 0, sta_depth_m <= SHELF_M, year %in% SERIES)
eff  <- effort %>% filter(sta_depth_m > 0, sta_depth_m <= SHELF_M, year %in% SERIES)
cpue <- recs %>% count(month, wt = n_total, name = "n_larvae") %>%
  complete(month = 1:12, fill = list(n_larvae = 0)) %>%
  left_join(eff %>% count(month, name = "n_tows"), by = "month") %>%
  mutate(per_100 = if_else(n_tows > 0, 100 * n_larvae / n_tows, NA_real_),
         month_lab = factor(month.abb[month], levels = month.abb))
write_csv(cpue, file.path(dir_derived, "cpue_by_month.csv"), na = "")
cpue %>% select(month_lab, n_larvae, n_tows, per_100)
```

September carries more sorted shelf tows than any other month, so in raw counts it looks like a
second spawning peak. Dividing by effort removes it.

The peak is not a footprint artefact either. Held to the Texas--Louisiana shelf alone, which is
sampled in every month, the margin widens rather than narrows.

```{r season-fixed-area}
tx <- effort %>% filter(region == "Texas-Louisiana shelf", year %in% SERIES) %>%
  count(month, name = "tows") %>%
  left_join(rates %>% filter(region == "Texas-Louisiana shelf", year %in% SERIES) %>%
              count(month, wt = n_total, name = "larvae"), by = "month") %>%
  mutate(rate = round(100 * coalesce(larvae, 0) / tows, 1))
tx %>% filter(month %in% c(5:9)) %>% select(month, tows, larvae, rate)
```

Abundance peaks in June but the smallest larvae peak in May, which fits a cohort spawned in or
before May rather than peak spawning in June. Two thirds of larvae were measured, so the bar is
split by the measured composition of that month.

```{r main_season, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 3.2}
mix <- lengths %>% inner_join(select(recs, v_c_p_s_cat, month), by = "v_c_p_s_cat") %>%
  count(month, size, name = "n_meas") %>%
  group_by(month) %>% mutate(share = n_meas / sum(n_meas)) %>% ungroup()

p_season <- cpue %>% select(month, month_lab, per_100) %>% inner_join(mix, by = "month") %>%
  ggplot(aes(month_lab, per_100 * share, fill = size)) +
  geom_col(colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = SIZE_COLS, name = NULL, drop = FALSE,
                    guide = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = substr(month.abb, 1, 1), drop = FALSE) +
  theme(legend.position = "right", legend.key.size = unit(8, "pt"),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 7)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Cobia larvae per 100 sorted\nshelf tows, 1982-2016")
p_season
```

# The two shelves

Gravid cobia are taken on the west Florida shelf, so an apparent scarcity of larvae there has to
be tested against season-matched effort rather than read off an annual map. West Florida takes
only about 12% of its shelf tows in June--July against 27% on the Texas--Louisiana shelf, because
the summer survey works west of 88 W. Everything here is restricted to June--July for that reason.

```{r shelf-cells}
peak_eff  <- effort %>% filter(month %in% PEAK)
peak_recs <- rates  %>% filter(month %in% PEAK)
CELL <- 0.5
cell <- function(x) mutate(x, cx = floor(lon / CELL) * CELL + CELL / 2,
                              cy = floor(lat / CELL) * CELL + CELL / 2)
cells <- cell(peak_eff) %>% count(cx, cy, name = "n_tows") %>%
  left_join(cell(peak_recs) %>% group_by(cx, cy) %>%
              summarise(n_larvae = sum(n_total), .groups = "drop"), by = c("cx", "cy")) %>%
  mutate(n_larvae = coalesce(n_larvae, 0), per_100 = 100 * n_larvae / n_tows,
         searched = n_tows >= 10)
sprintf("cells with >=10 June-July tows: %d; of those with no cobia: %d",
        sum(cells$searched), sum(cells$searched & cells$n_larvae == 0))
```

```{r main_shelf_maps, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.4}
frame <- list(geom_sf(data = filter(iso, depth_m == 200), colour = "grey35", linewidth = 0.3),
              geom_sf(data = land, fill = "grey85", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.2),
              map_frame, theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white")),
              theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 8.5, face = "plain")))
p_eff <- ggplot() + geom_tile(data = cells, aes(cx, cy, fill = n_tows)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10", option = "mako", direction = -1,
                       name = "Sorted June-July\ndeployments", breaks = c(1, 10, 100)) +
  frame + ggtitle("June-July sampling")
p_rate <- ggplot() +
  geom_tile(data = filter(cells, searched, n_larvae == 0), aes(cx, cy), fill = "grey88") +
  geom_tile(data = filter(cells, n_larvae > 0), aes(cx, cy, fill = per_100)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "sqrt", option = "inferno", direction = -1,
                       name = "Cobia larvae per\n100 deployments", breaks = c(10, 100, 300)) +
  frame + ggtitle("June-July catch rate")
p_eff | p_rate
```

A deployment is a station and a gear, which is what the denominator counts. Joining catch on
station alone would give each tow's larvae to both the bongo and the neuston row and double the
rate. Intervals are bootstrapped over tows, since larvae cluster within a tow and a Poisson
interval would be far too tight.

```{r shelf-rates}
tow_catch <- peak_recs %>% filter(year %in% SERIES) %>%
  mutate(gear_class = if_else(gear == "Neuston", "Neuston", "Bongo")) %>%
  group_by(v_c_p, gear_class) %>% summarise(n = sum(n_total), .groups = "drop")
set.seed(7)
boot_ci <- function(x, n = 2000) quantile(replicate(n, 100 * mean(sample(x, replace = TRUE))),
                                          c(0.025, 0.975))
reg <- peak_eff %>% filter(!is.na(region), year %in% SERIES) %>%
  select(v_c_p, gear, region) %>%
  left_join(tow_catch, by = c("v_c_p", "gear" = "gear_class")) %>%
  mutate(n = coalesce(n, 0)) %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(tows = n(), larvae = sum(n), rate = 100 * mean(n), pct_tows_with = 100 * mean(n > 0),
            ci = list(boot_ci(n)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(lo = map_dbl(ci, 1), hi = map_dbl(ci, 2), .keep = "unused")   # both limits from one set of resamples
write_csv(reg, file.path(dir_derived, "shelf_comparison.csv"))
reg
```

Not only season: the two are also comparable on depth, gear and spread over years, so the
difference is not a by-product of what was sampled.

```{r shelf-controls}
peak_eff %>% filter(!is.na(region), year %in% SERIES) %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(years = n_distinct(year), depth_med = round(median(sta_depth_m)),
            depth_q1 = round(quantile(sta_depth_m, .25)),
            depth_q3 = round(quantile(sta_depth_m, .75)),
            pct_bongo = round(100 * mean(gear == "Bongo")), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r main_shelf_bar, fig.width = 4, fig.height = 3.4}
p_bar <- ggplot(reg, aes(reorder(str_remove(region, " shelf"), -rate), rate)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#0072B2", colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.2, width = 0.6) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(y = hi, label = sprintf("%d tows\n%.0f larvae", tows, larvae)),
            vjust = -0.3, size = 2.5, lineheight = 0.95) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.28))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Larvae per 100 shelf tows,\nJune-July 1982-2016")
p_bar
```

# Size

```{r size-tables}
by_depth <- lengths %>%
  inner_join(select(gulf, v_c_p_s_cat, sta_depth_m, month), by = "v_c_p_s_cat") %>%
  filter(sta_depth_m > 0)
by_depth %>% mutate(where = if_else(sta_depth_m <= SHELF_M, "shelf", "off-shelf")) %>%
  group_by(where) %>% summarise(n = n(), median_mm = median(length_mm),
                                median_depth_m = round(median(sta_depth_m)))
by_depth %>% filter(month %in% 4:10) %>% count(month, size) %>%
  group_by(month) %>% mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n))) %>%
  select(-n) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = size, values_from = pct)
```

```{r main_size_depth, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 3.4}
p_size <- ggplot(by_depth, aes(sta_depth_m, length_mm, colour = size)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.45, size = 1.4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = SIZE_COLS, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(10, 30, 100, 300, 1000, 3000)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = SHELF_M, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  labs(x = "Station depth (m, log scale)", y = "Larval length (mm)")
p_size
```

The cut-off for the smallest class has no strong basis, so the shelf result is checked against it
rather than resting on it. It weakens gradually as larger and more dispersed larvae are swept in,
which is what should happen, and never reverses.

```{r explore_size_cutoff}
map_dfr(c(3, 3.2, 3.5, 4, 4.5, 5), function(cut) {
  keep <- lengths %>% group_by(v_c_p_s_cat) %>%
    summarise(hit = any(length_mm <= cut), .groups = "drop") %>% filter(hit)
  g <- gulf %>% filter(v_c_p_s_cat %in% keep$v_c_p_s_cat, !is.na(sta_depth_m))
  tibble(cut_mm = cut, larvae = sum(lengths$length_mm <= cut), records = nrow(g),
         pct_shelf = round(100 * mean(g$sta_depth_m <= SHELF_M)))
})
```

# Day and night

Pooled rates run higher at night, which could be larvae avoiding the net in daylight or larvae
sitting deeper by day. The two make opposite predictions. Avoidance should bite hardest on the
largest larvae, which see better and swim harder. Vertical movement should push catch between the
gears, since neuston fishes the top half-metre and bongo obliquely through the column.

```{r diel-table}
diel <- lengths %>%
  inner_join(rates %>% filter(!is.na(night)) %>% select(v_c_p_s_cat, gear, night),
             by = "v_c_p_s_cat") %>%
  count(gear, night, size, name = "larvae") %>%
  left_join(effort %>% filter(!is.na(night)) %>% count(gear, night, name = "tows"),
            by = c("gear", "night")) %>%
  mutate(per_100 = 100 * larvae / tows) %>%
  select(gear, size, night, per_100) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = night, values_from = per_100, names_prefix = "n") %>%
  transmute(gear, size, day = round(nFALSE, 2), night = round(nTRUE, 2),
            ratio = round(nTRUE / nFALSE, 2)) %>% arrange(gear, size)
write_csv(diel, file.path(dir_derived, "diel_by_gear_size.csv"))
diel
```

The neuston night:day ratio falls with larval size, which is backwards for net avoidance. And the
two gears move in opposite directions: bongo takes the smaller classes more by day while neuston
takes them more by night. That is what vertical movement between the gears' depths looks like.
The bongo large-larva cell is 0.01 against 0.05 per 100 tows, which is noise.

```{r explore_diel, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3.2}
diel %>% pivot_longer(c(day, night), names_to = "tod", values_to = "per_100") %>%
  ggplot(aes(size, per_100, fill = tod)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.2, width = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ gear, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(day = "#E8C547", night = "#2F4858"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("<5", "5-15", ">15")) +
  labs(x = "Larval length (mm)", y = "Measured larvae per 100 tows")
```

Daytime sampling on the early trawl surveys is a documented bias, corrected around 1995. Across
that break the daytime rate rises from 1.2 to 34.3 larvae per 100 tows while the night rate moves
only from 18.2 to 29.8, and a real change in abundance would move both alike, which points at the
early daytime samples rather than at the ocean. No interannual trend is plotted for that
reason, although catch rates do rise about tenfold from the 1980s to the 2010s.

```{r diel-era}
era <- effort %>% filter(!is.na(night), month %in% PEAK, sta_depth_m > 0,
                           sta_depth_m <= SHELF_M, year %in% SERIES) %>%
  mutate(era = if_else(year < 1995, "1982-1994", "1995-2016")) %>%
  count(era, night, name = "tows") %>%
  left_join(rates %>% filter(!is.na(night), month %in% PEAK, sta_depth_m > 0,
                               sta_depth_m <= SHELF_M, year %in% SERIES) %>%
              mutate(era = if_else(year < 1995, "1982-1994", "1995-2016")) %>%
              count(era, night, wt = n_total, name = "larvae"), by = c("era", "night")) %>%
  mutate(larvae = coalesce(larvae, 0), per_100 = round(100 * larvae / tows, 1))
write_csv(era, file.path(dir_derived, "diel_by_era.csv"))
era
```

# Temperature

Ditty and Shaw (1992) characterised Gulf cobia larvae by the surface temperature they were taken
at: 85% of their 76 larvae came from 25-30 degrees, mean 28.2, range 24.2-32.0. That is the one
axis where the archive can put their 76 larvae against a sampled background, because `STAREC`
carries a surface reading for nearly every station. The station table holds no salinity, so their
salinity result cannot be revisited here without pulling a further table.

A temperature at which larvae are caught is not a preference. Sampling itself is seasonal, so warm
water is oversampled relative to the year as a whole, and the comparison below is against the
temperatures actually fished rather than against the Gulf.

```{r temp-table}
temp_tows <- effort %>% filter(!is.na(temp_surf))
temp_pos  <- rates %>% filter(!is.na(temp_surf)) %>% uncount(n_total)

bind_rows(
  tibble(set = "All sorted tows",   t = temp_tows$temp_surf),
  tibble(set = "Larvae",            t = temp_pos$temp_surf)) %>%
  group_by(set) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = round(mean(t), 1), median = round(median(t), 1),
            min = round(min(t), 1), max = round(max(t), 1),
            pct_25_30 = round(100 * mean(t >= 25 & t <= 30), 1), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r explore_temp, fig.width = 5.5, fig.height = 3.2}
bind_rows(
  tibble(set = "All sorted tows", t = temp_tows$temp_surf),
  tibble(set = "Larvae",          t = temp_pos$temp_surf)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(t, after_stat(density), fill = set)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, position = "identity", alpha = 0.55,
                 colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("All sorted tows" = "grey60", "Larvae" = "#C1442E"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Surface temperature (C)", y = "Density")
```

```{r main_results, fig.width = 9.5, fig.height = 11.5}
(p_dist) / (p_eff | p_rate) / (p_season | p_bar | p_size) +
  plot_layout(heights = c(1.9, 1.5, 1.05)) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
```

# Checks

Each block states what should be true, computes it, and shows both sides so the comparison is
visible rather than reduced to a pass or fail.

## Extraction reproduces from the raw table

Counts taken straight from `ISARWK` should equal what the pipeline carried forward.

```{r check-extraction}
isarwk <- read_csv("data/raw/seamap/ISARWK.csv", col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                   show_col_types = FALSE, name_repair = "minimal") %>%
  rename_with(~ str_remove(.x, "^\ufeff"))
ALIQ_MULT <- c("1/1" = 1, "1/2" = 2, "1/4" = 4, "1/8" = 8)

raw <- isarwk %>% filter(str_detect(toupper(TAXON), "^RACHYCENTR")) %>%
  mutate(n = (coalesce(as.numeric(MEAS), 0) + coalesce(as.numeric(NOT_MEAS), 0)) *
             coalesce(ALIQ_MULT[ALIQUOT], 1))

tibble(quantity    = c("records", "larvae after aliquot correction", "sub-sampled records"),
       from_raw    = c(nrow(raw), sum(raw$n), sum(raw$ALIQUOT != "1/1")),
       in_pipeline = c(nrow(records), sum(records$n_total), sum(records$aliquot != "1/1"))) %>%
  mutate(agree = from_raw == in_pipeline)
```

An unanchored taxon match would also catch *Poromitra megalops*, a melamphaid sharing the species
epithet. These two lists should be identical.

```{r check-taxon}
tibble(anchored   = paste(sort(unique(raw$TAXON)), collapse = "; "),
       unanchored = isarwk %>% filter(str_detect(toupper(TAXON), "RACHYCENTR")) %>%
                      pull(TAXON) %>% unique() %>% sort() %>% paste(collapse = "; "))
```

## Station join

Every record should carry a station, and positions and dates should be possible.

```{r check-join}
tibble(quantity = c("records without a station", "latitude range", "longitude range",
                    "date range", "duplicated catalogue keys", "records outside the study box"),
       value = c(as.character(sum(is.na(records$lat))),
                 sprintf("%.1f to %.1f N", min(records$lat), max(records$lat)),
                 sprintf("%.1f to %.1f", min(records$lon), max(records$lon)),
                 sprintf("%s to %s", min(records$date), max(records$date)),
                 as.character(sum(duplicated(records$v_c_p_s_cat))),
                 as.character(nrow(records) - nrow(gulf))))
```

## The numerator belongs to the same pool as the denominator

Effort is sorted bongo and neuston deployments, so a larva taken any other way has no matching
denominator. These are the records held out of every rate.

```{r check-excluded}
gulf %>%
  mutate(why = case_when(!gear %in% c("Bongo", "Neuston") ~ paste("gear:", gear),
                         !sort_ist %in% SORTED            ~ "not flagged sorted",
                         TRUE                             ~ "in the rates")) %>%
  count(why, wt = n_total, name = "larvae")
```

Recomputing the monthly numerator from scratch, with all four filters applied, should land on the
number the rates were built from.

```{r check-numerator}
tibble(source = c("rebuilt here", "used in the monthly rates"),
       larvae = c(gulf %>% filter(gear %in% c("Bongo", "Neuston"), sort_ist %in% SORTED,
                                  sta_depth_m > 0, sta_depth_m <= SHELF_M,
                                  year %in% SERIES) %>% pull(n_total) %>% sum(),
                  sum(cpue$n_larvae)))
```

## Lengths

Coverage is uneven and worst in the largest tows, which is where a size class rests on fewest
measurements.

```{r check-lengths}
tibble(quantity = c("larvae measured", "larvae counted", "coverage",
                    "tows holding >10 larvae", "of those, under half measured",
                    "length range", "measured exceeds counted",
                    "size classes do not sum to measured"),
       value = c(sum(gulf$n_meas, na.rm = TRUE), sum(gulf$n_total),
                 sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * sum(gulf$n_meas, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(gulf$n_total)),
                 sum(gulf$n_total > 10),
                 sum(gulf$n_total > 10 & gulf$n_meas / gulf$n_total < 0.5, na.rm = TRUE),
                 sprintf("%.1f to %.1f mm", min(lengths$length_mm), max(lengths$length_mm)),
                 sum(gulf$n_meas > gulf$n_total, na.rm = TRUE),
                 sum(gulf$n_small + gulf$n_mid + gulf$n_big != gulf$n_meas, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
         as.character())
```

## Depth

Station depth is recorded in fathoms and converted. An independent bathymetry gives a check on
whether the conversion is right: agreement should be near-perfect, and a missed conversion would
show as a constant offset on the log scale.

```{r check-depth}
chk <- gulf %>% filter(sta_depth_m > 0)
chk$etopo_m <- -terra::extract(rast(as.xyz(b), type = "xyz", crs = "EPSG:4326"),
                               as.matrix(chk[, c("lon", "lat")]))[, 1]
chk <- filter(chk, etopo_m > 0)
tibble(stations = nrow(chk),
       correlation_log_depth = round(cor(log10(chk$sta_depth_m), log10(chk$etopo_m)), 3),
       median_ratio = round(median(chk$sta_depth_m / chk$etopo_m), 2),
       disagree_over_fourfold = sum(chk$sta_depth_m / chk$etopo_m > 4 |
                                    chk$sta_depth_m / chk$etopo_m < 0.25))
```

## Does the seasonal peak survive the controls?

The survey does not sample the same places, or at the same hours, in every month. If the June and
July peak were an artefact of either, it should weaken when the area is held fixed or when day and
night tows are separated. It does neither.

```{r check-season-controls}
tod <- effort %>% filter(!is.na(night), sta_depth_m > 0, sta_depth_m <= SHELF_M,
                         year %in% SERIES) %>%
  count(month, night, name = "tows") %>%
  left_join(rates %>% filter(!is.na(night), sta_depth_m > 0, sta_depth_m <= SHELF_M,
                             year %in% SERIES) %>%
              count(month, night, wt = n_total, name = "larvae"), by = c("month", "night")) %>%
  mutate(rate = 100 * coalesce(larvae, 0) / tows)

tibble(control = c("all Gulf shelf, pooled", "Texas-Louisiana shelf only",
                   "day tows only", "night tows only"),
       june_july = c(max(cpue$per_100[cpue$month %in% PEAK]),
                     max(tx$rate[tx$month %in% PEAK]),
                     max(tod$rate[tod$month %in% PEAK & !tod$night]),
                     max(tod$rate[tod$month %in% PEAK & tod$night])),
       september = c(cpue$per_100[cpue$month == 9], tx$rate[tx$month == 9],
                     tod$rate[tod$month == 9 & !tod$night],
                     tod$rate[tod$month == 9 & tod$night])) %>%
  mutate(across(june_july:september, ~ round(.x, 1)), ratio = round(june_july / september, 1))
```

## Does the shelf difference survive them?

West Florida takes a far smaller share of its tows in the spawning months, which is what made an
all-month comparison misleading. Within June and July the two regions are comparable on depth,
gear and years sampled, so the difference is not a by-product of what was sampled.

```{r check-shelf-controls}
effort %>% filter(!is.na(region), sta_depth_m <= SHELF_M) %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(shelf_tows = n(), pct_in_june_july = round(100 * mean(month %in% PEAK)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(effort %>% filter(!is.na(region), month %in% PEAK, year %in% SERIES) %>%
              group_by(region) %>%
              summarise(years = n_distinct(year), depth_median = round(median(sta_depth_m)),
                        pct_bongo = round(100 * mean(gear == "Bongo")), .groups = "drop"),
            by = "region") %>%
  left_join(reg %>% select(region, rate, lo, hi) %>%
              mutate(across(rate:hi, ~ round(.x, 1))), by = "region")
```

## Why no interannual trend is fitted

Catch rates rise roughly tenfold between the 1980s and the 2010s. Daytime sampling on the early
trawl surveys was a known bias, addressed in the mid 1990s. If the rise were real, day and night
rates should move together across that break. The day rate moves about 29-fold and the night rate
about 1.6-fold, so the rise tracks the sampling.

```{r check-trend}
era %>% select(era, night, tows, larvae, per_100) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = era, values_from = c(tows, larvae, per_100)) %>%
  mutate(fold_change = round(`per_100_1995-2016` / `per_100_1982-1994`, 1))
```

## Surface temperature sentinels

`TEMP_SSURF` carries zeros where no reading was taken. Left in, they would drag the mean down and
invent cold-water records. The raw column is checked against the filtered one.

```{r check-temp}
raw_t <- read_csv(file.path("data/raw/seamap", "STAREC.csv"),
                  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                  show_col_types = FALSE, name_repair = "minimal") %>%
  rename_with(~ str_remove(.x, "^\ufeff")) %>%
  transmute(t = as.numeric(TEMP_SSURF))

tibble(check = c("stations in STAREC", "temperature recorded", "zero or below 5",
                 "above 36", "kept"),
       n = c(nrow(raw_t), sum(!is.na(raw_t$t)), sum(raw_t$t < 5, na.rm = TRUE),
             sum(raw_t$t > 36, na.rm = TRUE),
             sum(raw_t$t >= 5 & raw_t$t <= 36, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

## June and July sampling ends in 2016

The records run to 2024, but plankton sampling on the summer trawl survey stopped after 2016. Any
monthly comparison that ignores this sets June and July over one span of years against September
over another.

```{r check-series-end}
effort %>% filter(month %in% PEAK, sta_depth_m > 0, sta_depth_m <= SHELF_M) %>%
  count(year, name = "june_july_shelf_tows") %>%
  filter(year >= 2013) %>%
  full_join(tibble(year = 2013:max(gulf$year)), by = "year") %>%
  arrange(year) %>%
  mutate(june_july_shelf_tows = coalesce(june_july_shelf_tows, 0L))
```

## Station times are read in their recorded zone

`TIME_ZN` shifts from local time to GMT over the series. If the conversion is right, the share of
tows classed as night should hold roughly steady from decade to decade rather than jump when the
logging convention changes.

```{r check-time-zone}
effort %>% mutate(decade = 10 * (year %/% 10),
                  zone = recode(as.character(time_zn), "1" = "EST", "2" = "EDT", "3" = "CST", "4" = "CDT",
                                "5" = "AST", "6" = "ADT", "8" = "GMT", .default = "other")) %>%
  group_by(decade) %>%
  summarise(tows = n(), pct_gmt = round(100 * mean(zone == "GMT")),
            pct_local = round(100 * mean(zone %in% c("EST", "EDT", "CST", "CDT", "AST", "ADT"))),
            pct_night = round(100 * mean(night, na.rm = TRUE)),
            no_time = sum(is.na(night)), .groups = "drop")
```
